role.en: Protestant pastor of Wilhelmsfeld, Germany; Rizal's host in 1886
role.fil: Pastor Protestante ng Wilhelmsfeld, Alemanya; nagpatuloy kay Rizal noong 1886
role.de: Protestantischer Pfarrer von Wilhelmsfeld, Deutschland; Rizals Gastgeber im Jahr 1886

portrait.alt: Grainy photograph of Pastor Karl Ullmer, a bearded man seated in a dark suit with a book resting on his lap

quote.en: The Filipino public received “Noli Me Tangere” very well and the entire edition is sold out. The government and the church have strictly forbidden it, but that made it sought after and sold even more… while the enemies burned copies of my book, my friends bought every copy… The booksellers made a lot of money; I alone did not.
quote.fil: Napakainam ang pagtanggap ng publikong Pilipino sa “Noli Me Tangere” at naubos ang buong edisyon. Mahigpit itong ipinagbawal ng pamahalaan at ng simbahan, ngunit dahil doon ay lalo itong hinanap at naipagbili… habang sinusunog ng mga kaaway ang mga sipi ng aking aklat, binili ng aking mga kaibigan ang bawat sipi… Malaki ang kinita ng mga naglalako ng aklat; ako lamang ang hindi.
quote.de: Das philippinische Publikum hat „Noli Me Tangere“ sehr gut aufgenommen, und die gesamte Auflage ist ausverkauft. Regierung und Kirche haben es streng verboten, doch dadurch wurde es nur umso begehrter und verkaufte sich noch besser… während die Feinde Exemplare meines Buches verbrannten, kauften meine Freunde jedes einzelne auf… Die Buchhändler haben viel Geld verdient; nur ich nicht.

quoteSource.en: Rizal to K. Ullmer, London, 8 June 1888
quoteSource.fil: Rizal kay K. Ullmer, London, 8 Hunyo 1888
quoteSource.de: Rizal an K. Ullmer, London, 8. Juni 1888

bio.en:
Rizal's stay in Wilhelmsfeld may have been a walk in the park in the literal and figurative sense, contrary to what he would face after Noli Me Tangere was released. In his brief respite in the small town, Rizal lived with Protestant Pastor Karl Ullmer and his family in the vicarage of Wilhelmsfeld. Pastor Ullmer was the administrator of Wilhelmsfeld Parish from 1878 to 1888.

Rizal's stay with the family allowed him to deepen his fluency in German. To encourage Rizal, Ullmer introduced him to William Tell, a work by German writer Friedrich von Schiller. Their daily early morning discussions regarding this literature were instrumental in Rizal's mastery of the German language. During his stay, Rizal would also accompany Ullmer during walks around town and the vicarage. It was also during this time that he completed the last chapters of the Noli Me Tangere, which did not shy from criticizing the Spanish friars due to the issue of secularization of the Filipino priests.

The Pastor, who espoused ideas of liberalism, was antithetical to the men of religion depicted by Rizal in his novel. As such, in his letters to Ullmer and during his recollection of his time in Wilhelmsfeld when he was already in exile in Dapitan, Rizal remembered his stay with the Pastor and the friendships he gained positively. It was there that Rizal found understanding “despite [his] brown skin.”

Pastor Ullmer learned of Rizal's death after reading it in a newspaper. Years later, the descendants of the Pastor, Fritz and Hans Ullmer, donated the objects that were used by Rizal to the Philippine government and Rizal's kin. These objects included letters, an original copy of the first edition of the Noli Me Tangere with a written dedication, and several notes and sketches of Rizal, among others.
bio.fil:
Ang pananatili ni Rizal sa Wilhelmsfeld ay maaaring naging tila paglalakad sa parke sa literal at patalinghagang paraan, salungat sa kanyang haharapin matapos mailabas ang Noli Me Tangere. Sa kanyang maikling pamamahinga sa maliit na bayan, nanirahan si Rizal kasama ang Pastor Protestanteng si Karl Ullmer at ang kanyang pamilya sa pastoran ng Wilhelmsfeld. Si Pastor Ullmer ang tagapangasiwa ng Parokya ng Wilhelmsfeld mula 1878 hanggang 1888.

Ang pananatili ni Rizal sa pamilya ay nagbigay-daan upang palalimin ang kanyang katatasan sa Aleman. Upang palakasin ang loob ni Rizal, ipinakilala sa kanya ni Ullmer ang William Tell, isang akda ng manunulat na Alemang si Friedrich von Schiller. Ang araw-araw nilang talakayan tuwing madaling-araw hinggil sa panitikang ito ay naging mahalaga sa pagkadalubhasa ni Rizal sa wikang Aleman. Sa kanyang pananatili, sumasama rin si Rizal kay Ullmer sa mga paglalakad sa paligid ng bayan at ng pastoran. Sa panahon ding ito tinapos niya ang mga huling kabanata ng Noli Me Tangere, na hindi nag-atubiling pumuna sa mga prayleng Espanyol dahil sa isyu ng sekularisasyon ng mga paring Pilipino.

Ang Pastor, na nagtataguyod ng mga ideya ng liberalismo, ay kasalungat ng mga tao ng relihiyong inilarawan ni Rizal sa kanyang nobela. Kaya naman, sa kanyang mga liham kay Ullmer at sa kanyang paggunita sa kanyang panahon sa Wilhelmsfeld noong siya ay nasa pagkatapon na sa Dapitan, positibong naalala ni Rizal ang kanyang pananatili kasama ang Pastor at ang mga pagkakaibigang natamo niya. Doon natagpuan ni Rizal ang pag-unawa “sa kabila ng [kanyang] kayumangging balat.”

Nalaman ni Pastor Ullmer ang pagkamatay ni Rizal matapos itong mabasa sa pahayagan. Makalipas ang mga taon, ipinagkaloob ng mga inapo ng Pastor, sina Fritz at Hans Ullmer, ang mga bagay na ginamit ni Rizal sa pamahalaan ng Pilipinas at sa kamag-anak ni Rizal. Kabilang sa mga bagay na ito ang mga liham, isang orihinal na sipi ng unang edisyon ng Noli Me Tangere na may nakasulat na alay, at ilang tala at sketch ni Rizal, bukod sa iba pa.
bio.de:
Rizals Aufenthalt in Wilhelmsfeld mag im wörtlichen wie im übertragenen Sinne ein Spaziergang gewesen sein – anders als das, was ihm nach dem Erscheinen des Noli Me Tangere bevorstand. In dieser kurzen Ruhepause in dem kleinen Ort lebte Rizal beim protestantischen Pfarrer Karl Ullmer und seiner Familie im Pfarrhaus von Wilhelmsfeld. Pfarrer Ullmer verwaltete die Gemeinde Wilhelmsfeld von 1878 bis 1888.

Der Aufenthalt bei der Familie erlaubte es Rizal, seine Deutschkenntnisse zu vertiefen. Um ihn zu ermutigen, machte Ullmer ihn mit Wilhelm Tell bekannt, einem Werk des deutschen Dichters Friedrich von Schiller. Ihre täglichen Gespräche am frühen Morgen über dieses Werk trugen entscheidend dazu bei, dass Rizal die deutsche Sprache meisterte. Während seines Aufenthalts begleitete Rizal Ullmer auch auf Spaziergängen durch den Ort und um das Pfarrhaus. In dieser Zeit vollendete er ebenfalls die letzten Kapitel des Noli Me Tangere, das die spanischen Ordensleute wegen der Frage der Säkularisierung der philippinischen Priester unverhohlen kritisierte.

Der Pfarrer, der liberalen Gedanken zuneigte, war das Gegenbild jener Geistlichen, die Rizal in seinem Roman zeichnete. Entsprechend erinnerte sich Rizal in seinen Briefen an Ullmer und in seinen Rückblicken auf die Zeit in Wilhelmsfeld, als er schon im Exil in Dapitan war, mit Wärme an den Aufenthalt beim Pfarrer und an die dort gewonnenen Freundschaften. Dort fand Rizal Verständnis „trotz [seiner] braunen Haut“.

Von Rizals Tod erfuhr Pfarrer Ullmer aus der Zeitung. Jahre später schenkten die Nachkommen des Pfarrers, Fritz und Hans Ullmer, die von Rizal benutzten Gegenstände der philippinischen Regierung und Rizals Angehörigen. Dazu gehörten Briefe, ein Originalexemplar der ersten Ausgabe des Noli Me Tangere mit handschriftlicher Widmung sowie mehrere Notizen und Zeichnungen Rizals.
